title: Tendon, Bone, Blood, Muscle Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Aarav lifts a heavy school bag and feels his arm work. What joins a muscle to a bone? And how can blood, a liquid, be a tissue?

You will see what makes a tissue connective (cells, collagen and elastin fibres, matrix), then a zoom ladder from the upper arm to the tendon and its parallel collagen fibres. We sort connective tissue step by step: areolar, adipose, dense (tendons and ligaments), cartilage and bone, then blood as a fluid connective tissue made in the bone marrow. Muscle fibres contract and relax, and we compare skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle with a pause and think. Then a worked example naming three body parts, the tendon vs ligament exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. Note: This topic (animal tissues) is not in the current rationalised NCERT text but is in the ISC (CISCE) Class 11 syllabus.

This is Episode 57 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
